answer.justification: The recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) is closely related to the inferior thyroid artery, often crossing it or running in close proximity within the tracheoesophageal groove. During thyroid surgery, ligation of the inferior thyroid artery carries a significant risk of injury to the RLN. Damage to the RLN leads to paralysis of the intrinsic muscles of the larynx (excluding the cricothyroid), resulting in vocal cord dysfunction and the characteristic symptom of hoarseness.
